claim_boundary: Local exact-source representation oracle only; no same-run BDC sibling, create, locality, reader/native/recovery, product, release or external-frontier credit.
decision: ADVANCE_COORDER_ORACLE. Making regular-row order equal the deterministic CMPNXBD2 member order removes both the duplicate per-file SHA and the explicit member index. On exact accepted sources this further improves the conservative complete-semantic projection to 72,896 B on Boundary (201 B below Zstd-19) and 1,688,056 B on Shifted (6,618 B below Zstd-19). This remains lower-rung representation evidence only.
kill_or_narrow: same-run complete coordered semantic sibling fails exact filesystem reconstruction or corruption rejection
Boundary complete stored bytes are >= strongest-current Zstd-19
regular-row implicit ordering cannot be made deterministic for hardlinks/duplicate content under the actual FS grammar
complete create/locality/decode-unit/native/recovery cost makes the representation non-Pareto
question: Can manifest row order itself own the path->BDC-member mapping, eliminating both duplicate SHA and explicit member index?
representation: regular manifest rows are emitted in exact CMPNXBD2 member order and store [logical_size] only; nonregular rows remain deterministic metadata and consume no member slot
